service ecosystems are the result of the interactions among the actors, institutions and technologies that are integrated in service systems.
service ecosystems are a network of actors that are interdependent through resource integration and that the formation of service systems is influenced by social factors, such as institutions.
the service-ecosystem framework is a useful way to understand the (re) formation of service systems and the value they cocreate.

understanding the processes of value creation and exchange in service systems, and the (co)creation and (re)formation thereof.
the (re)configuration of service systems and how this process can be facilitated through resource integration and value cocreation.
the development of an S-D logic, service- ecosystem view of service systems.

service systems are the fundamental building block of the service-dominant logic of service.
the service-ecosystem approach is a useful and promising framework for understanding value cocreation and service-systems (re)formation.
the service ecosystem approach to value cocreation and (re)formation is a useful and promising framework for studying and managing service.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
service ecosystems are formed by the integration of resources, which is enabled by technology and influenced by the social and institutional environment.
service-ecosystem view is an important framework for understanding how service systems are formed and re-formed, and how value is cocreated in the process.
we have developed a service-ecosystem approach to studying value co-creation and the (re-)formation of service systems.

service ecosystems are dynamic and complex, and that value cocreation and (re)formation are emergent processes.
